text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your history of chronic bronchitis and recent weight loss alongside leg swelling, have you noticed any shortness of breath, fever, or cough with blood? Additionally, have you experienced any changes in your urine output or noticed any abdominal discomfort?

I need to determine the underlying cause of this kidney dysfunction, so do you have a history of high blood pressure or diabetes, and have you noticed any foamy urine or skin itching?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic Syndrome (likely Membranous Nephropathy given age and gender).

The combination of heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and lipid abnormalities confirms nephrotic syndrome; your age and gender make Membranous Nephropathy the leading suspicion. Given the absence of diabetes or hypertension, I need to rule out malignancy or other secondary causes.
